topic: sub:12|Relative frequency and probability|Number of outcomes for an experiment

parts.latex: A taxi number plate begins with a letter T and is followed by 4 digits. Each digit can be one of the numbers $0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ or $9$. How many different number plates of this type are there?

solutions.latex:
The plate begins with the fixed letter T, so there is only 1 choice for the first position.

Each of the 4 digits can be any of 10 digits, with repeats allowed.
$$1\times 10\times 10\times 10\times 10=10\times 10\times 10\times 10$$
Option A and option C do not allow repeated digits, and option D includes 26 choices for the letter, which is fixed.

$$\therefore\ 10\times 10\times 10\times 10 \text{ plates}$$

parts.latex:
Postcodes in Australia are made up of four digits e.g. 2040.

How many different postcodes beginning with 2 are possible?

solutions.latex:
The postcode has the form $2\_\_\_$, so the first digit is fixed.

Each of the other three places can be any of $10$ digits.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number} &= 10\times10\times10 \\ &= 1000 \end{aligned}$$
